cost_findings: matmul J +5.4137% and T +14.1957% trigger predeclared diagnostic flags; A +0.1072% does not erase J/T costs.
matmul process allocation median increases only 336/344/336 bytes; no evidence of per-inner-iteration token allocation. Numeric-list MIR/CIL 1Create/2Read/1Append preserved.
math_module whole-process allocation grows by exactly 56000304 bytes median in each backend, about 108.8%; all three allocation flags retained.

Actual candidate AOT CaptureModuleMethod calls RhpNewFast. Captured CallMethod1 branch calls RhpNewPtrArrayFast with length 1, then CallValue. One million calls times conventional x64 24-byte token plus 32-byte array predicts 56MB, consistent with measured delta; this is structural inference, not allocation-stack profiling.
Actual AOT matmul method has two CaptureModuleMethod call sites, outside the specialized numeric read/append path; method size grows 45 bytes. Generic PIC entry also has token checking.

AOT machine code does not establish JIT inlining/layout or uniquely explain J/T slowdown. No extra performance samples; the separately labeled two-process local JIT diagnostic is not part of the 36-process experiment.
limitations: Linux x64 same-runner bounded observation only; not Windows/macOS performance.
Three short warmups do not establish Tier1 steady state.
Allocation/GC/heap/RSS are whole-process including 3 warmups, 7 samples and checks, not per-kernel allocation.
AOT JIT counters are N/A in interpreted results, original raw stats retained in artifact.
All favorable and adverse points retained. Diagnostic thresholds do not authorize restoring incorrect Python evaluation order.
Build durations are end-to-end and may include restore/cache effects.
Raw artifact retention follows workflow policy; this compact report is not a promise of permanent raw storage.

local_jit_diagnostic.scope: Separate authorized structural diagnostic, not a performance sample or CI slowdown attribution
local_jit_diagnostic.conclusion: Actual call, inlining, stack and layout changes exist; a different local CPU and absent CI JIT disassembly/counters prevent assigning the CI 14.2% slowdown to any single mechanism.
